heroHeadline: China Establishes 16+ Vessel Dual-Ring Perimeter at Scarborough Shoal; USCG Midgett-PCG Joint Presence Day 4; AUKUS Ministerial Announces First UUV Project at Shangri-La Dialogue
heroSubtitle: China escalated maritime pressure at Scarborough Shoal on May 31, 2026, deploying a dual-ring perimeter of at least 16 vessels — 9 China Coast Guard vessels forming an outer cordon at 20-40 nautical miles and 7 maritime militia vessels forming an inner ring at 5-17 nautical miles — as the Philippines publicly warned of a threat to the feature. The deployment is concurrent with a five-day joint maritime presence operation by USCG Midgett (WMSL-757, ~4,500 tons) and PCG BRP Melchora Aquino near Scarborough Shoal (May 28-31), representing the most direct US-Philippine coast guard bilateral presence at the disputed feature since 2023. China's Xiang Yang Hong 33 research vessel entered its 25th consecutive day of unauthorized presence near Pag-asa (Thitu) Island on May 31, as Beijing's diplomatic silence on the Philippines' UNCLOS Article 246 note verbale extended to a 20th consecutive day — the longest unanswered Philippine diplomatic instrument under the Marcos administration. At the 2026 Shangri-La Dialogue in Singapore on May 30, AUKUS defense ministers (US SecDef Hegseth, UK DefSec Healey, Australian DefMin Marles) announced the inaugural Pillar II signature project — joint development of uncrewed undersea vehicle (UUV) payloads with delivery beginning 2027 — while confirming Australia will receive secondhand Virginia-class submarines. The Philippines' three active West Philippine Sea standoffs persist: (1) Xiang Yang Hong 33 near Pag-asa (Day 25, UNCLOS silence Day 20); (2) Scarborough Shoal (16+ vessel perimeter, unanswered marine nature reserve claim, USCG Midgett presence); (3) Second Thomas Shoal (CCG blockade posture). China's Scarborough perimeter formation represents the most comprehensive simultaneous pressure package at a single contested South China Sea feature since the 2012 de facto seizure.
